head: Branch tip 6252a08d (12 commits, 40 files, +8727/-16 vs origin/main; worktree clean, nothing pushed). All five verdict findings close — both blockers and all three shoulds — and I raced each one myself against the tip rather than trusting the fix round's own cells: an independent probe script (scratchpad rc653.cjs) drove the real doors as a real bookkeeper on 55511 and reproduced every reviewer measurement with the opposite answer. Because the migration changed I rebuilt rig653r from scratch with mkrig.sh (fresh cluster, 0 clara roles at prestate, so 0154's cluster-global role census passed), created clara_653r, applied the whole chain (194 applied, #653 prestate clean + tail OK), re-applied (0 new), seeded, and ran both batteries there: 28/28. No regressions anywhere: typecheck 0, lint 0, frozen-workflows OK (281 files / 51 modules), parts-parity OK, frozen-evaluators OK (9) on both rigs, whole apps/web suite 3752/3750/0 fail/2 skip exit 0 (653-N3's thread-live-clarify flake did NOT fire for me either), runtime occurrence e2e PASS 1-5, and both Playwright walks green in ONE real-harness run (15/15 = 6 prepayments-walk + 9 plans-walk), which also closes 653-N2's evidence gap. Non-blocking observations for the orchestrator, none of them new defects: (1) the B2 wall is NEGATIVE only — I confirmed on the rig that this estate carries exactly two account classes (receivable/payable, 27 each) and zero bank-stamped accounts, so genuine prepaid accounts (NULL class) still pass, which is the fix round's own follow-up 1; (2) clara.create_prepayment_schedule is the ONLY function in the schema that inserts into clara.prepayment_schedules (measured), so the wall has no bypass path; (3) the attentionTruncated copy says "Showing the {shown} most recent" using BOTH arms' combined row count while the cap is per-arm — cosmetic only; (4) follow-up 2 (0154's `= 14` role census over a cluster-global catalog) is corroborated by my run: a fresh CLUSTER applies cleanly, which is exactly the workaround it names. rig653r/55611 is left online carrying clara_653r (194 migrations + seed) for whoever closes the wave.
closed: 653-B1 (blocker) — the form no longer fabricates an authority. prepayment-form.tsx now renders a required Select over lib/plans/api.ts's listAuthorityCandidates bound to a fifth draft field, the `?? draft.sourceEntryId` fallback is deleted, validatePrepaymentDraft refuses `authorityRequired`, prepaymentRefusalKey maps authority_ref_unresolved -> refusalAuthorityUnresolved, en.json carries the six strings, and prepayments-mock.mjs refuses any payload not citing PREPAY.workId. MY OWN measurement on 55511: the door called with exactly the old payload -> CLR10 {reason: authority_ref_unresolved}; `select count(*) from clara.accounting_work w join clara.journal_entries j on j.id=w.id` -> 0; the SAME call citing a real accounting_work id -> accepted (plan 33938a8b, kind amortisation_schedule). create_accounting_plan's resolver (read from the live catalog) only checks existence + firm/client tenancy, so every row the picker offers resolves. Unit cell prepayments.authority reads the REQUEST BODY (no door call without an instruction, focus on prepayment-authority, p_authority_ref.id === WORK != p_source_entry). db cell p653.schedule.authority_ref_unresolved passes. Walk cell prepayments.walk.refusal passes and now selects the instruction.

653-B2 (blocker) — a receivable can no longer be amortised, and the band no longer advertises one. The door runs clara._adj_line_eligibility_breach on the prepaid leg right after reading it off the evaluator output and refuses 0140's own prepayment_source_unfit with axis=prepaid_account_ineligible; arm B carries the identical predicate in its WHERE. MY OWN measurement on 55511 against a leftover approved, document-bound Dr-374-C56 invoice (account_class='receivable', live service period on its document): door -> CLR10 {reason: prepayment_source_unfit, axis: prepaid_account_ineligible, prepaid_account_code: 374-C56, breach: {axis: control_account, account_class: receivable}}, 0 schedules written; arm B lists it: FALSE, while the genuine 19000001 recognition is still listed. The helper (read from the catalog) ignores debit/credit and judges unknown/inactive/control-class/bank/reserved-role, so the bank and reserved cases are closed by the same rule. db cells p653.schedule.prepaid_leg_ineligible and p653.attention.arm_b_ineligible pass on both rigs.

653-S1 (should) — each arm is ordered before it is cut and the envelope says when the cut bit. Both arms became `with cand_x ... select jsonb_agg(... order by sk desc), (select count(*) from cand_x) > 50 from (select ... order by sk desc limit 50)`, and the envelope gained refusing_truncated / unscheduled_truncated / cap. MY OWN measurement on a client carrying 52 arm-B candidates: 50 rows returned, cap 50, unscheduled_truncated=true, refusing_truncated=false, first row IS the newest candidate (2026-06-20), order strictly descending, the oldest candidate (2026-05-01) absent. db cell p653.attention.window and two web render cells (truncated shows the notice, untruncated shows nothing) pass.

653-S2 (should) — the raced loser is answered in the lane's own words. The INSERT is wrapped in `exception when unique_violation` which re-reads the winner and re-raises the same CLR13 prepayment_schedule_exists payload with raced:true. MY OWN two-session race on 55511 (two clara_authenticated sessions as one bookkeeper, different op keys, B witnessed queued behind A via pg_stat_activity.wait_event_type='Lock' = true): loser -> code CLR13, detail {reason: prepayment_schedule_exists, schedule_id: 3ff1f6e5-..., source_entry: 0e806572-..., raced: true}; NOT 23505 and no constraint name; exactly one schedule survives. db cell p653.schedule.duplicate_race passes.

653-S3 (should) — the two drifted titles now say what they measure, and the promised negatives exist. p653.attention.arm_b's last leg is renamed to the status filter it actually drives (unapprovedEntry is a DRAFT debiting the prepaid asset), the negative the old title promised is the new p653.attention.arm_b_ineligible (which doubles as B2's regression guard), and p653.schedule.target_ineligible gained the control-account leg it had promised, recording that not_expense_class fires first from the expense side. Verified by reading the diff and by 28/28 green on the from-scratch cluster (schedule 18/18 + occurrences 10/10 on the lane rig, was 15 + 8).

F1 (note) — the CI step's env assignments regained the per-line `\` continuation of its #640 sibling immediately above it. I extracted the whole 223-line run: body of that composite-action step (sed lines 62-284, dedented) and `bash -n` exits 0, so the block is syntactically valid as well as formatted to parity.

F2 (note) — left as-is, correctly. `git diff cc2beaa5..HEAD -- apps/web/e2e/plans-mock.mjs` is EMPTY, so the sibling lane's mock did not move again this round; it stays the integration pass's call, and its behaviour is now proven by the plans-walk run below.

653-N1 (note) — the fix round took a different route (rebuilt clara_653 on 55511 from a true prestate) with a sound reason. I did the rig653r half myself instead: recreated the cluster with mkrig.sh (prestate: 0 clara roles), created clara_653r, applied 194 migrations with #653 prestate/tail both raised, re-applied for 0 new, seeded 2 files, and ran both batteries there: 28/28.

653-N2 (note) — the evidence gap is closed. plans-walk ran in the same real-harness invocation as prepayments-walk: 9/9 passed, so plans-mock.mjs's readCachedJson refactor does not move #640's own walk.

653-N3 (note) — not reproduced. My whole apps/web unit run was 3752 tests / 3750 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped, exit 0; components/clara/thread-live-clarify.test.tsx passed inside the suite, so there is no second run to report.
